Three amendments passed into the version of the Senate Bill that passed:

• Baldwin: Preserves many state-law rights/remedies
• Scott: Requires disclosure of foreign funding in college sports
• Moody: Raises the conference membership cap from 19 to 20
This amendment was 3 votes away from passing. Would have completely altered college sports if passed into law.
The Senate College Sports bill will pass handily. 3 amendments made it in today. It awaits its fate in the House, not currently scheduled to reconvene before Election Day.
The 2nd Booker amendment failed, 47-52, which means they’re finally voting on the actual bill now lol.

The Booker amendment to raise the maximum cap for the athlete health fund from $100M to $200M is going to pass with a few Senators out tonight. Anything past $100M would come from the P4 conferences.
The amendment to increase the cap on teams in conferences from 19 to 20 teams has passed. Big news for potential realignment considerations.
Ashley Moody introduces her amendment to increase the conference cap from 19 to 20 teams. She references 4-0 USF and 4-0 Miami, as well as Florida State, as schools that might benefit.
The ticket increase cap amendment fails. It needed 60 votes to pass and has reached 41 nos.

In introducing his amendment, Senator Kennedy describes the current Senate bill as doing something for everyone, including schools, donors, coaches, and players, except for the fans. The amendment is a form of ticket rent control that would cap ticket increases at 4%/year.
The Paul amendment to basically replace the entire PCSA with a much smaller bill fails.

The Scott amendment has now passed, and requires all funding greater than $600 from foreign sources to be reported. Would apply to things like FSU exploring a partnership with the Saudi Public Investment Fund.

Of the 7 amendments that will be voted on tonight before final passage, one that may be most interesting to many comes from Senator Ashley Moody (Florida) and would raise the cap on conference size from 19 to 20 teams. Voted on 5th tonight. 👀

So this is interesting ...

• From 2000-09, every first-round QB made it thru three seasons with the team that drafted him.

• From 2010-24, seven (Tim Tebow, Brandon Weeden, Johnny Manziel, Josh Rosen, Trey Lance, Kenny Pickett, JJ McCarthy) haven't.

Seems pretty relevant.

The Giants and Vikings tried like hell to trade into the third pick to get Drake Maye in 2024. The Giants then decided to punt on the QB class. The Vikings took JJ McCarthy. And now McCarthy is traded from one to the other.

Drafting QBs—not a perfect science.

Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles says QB Baker Mayfield will miss at least three weeks with his right thumb injury. Could’ve been worse—Mayfield avoided a UCL injury that could’ve take him out for more than a month.

Giants coach John Harbaugh obviously has good background on JJ McCarthy from his brother—even got to see a few of McCarthy’s games at Michigan from the sideline. Still just 23, McCarthy will come in to back up Jameis Winston initially, and we’ll see where it goes from there.
